question: Should OpenClaw core accept this broad agent-continuation architecture now, require a split maintainer-sponsored design before merge, or close/defer it outside core?
rationale: The PR adds a large optional core orchestration system with new config, session state, trusted cross-session context injection, and protocol/runtime changes; automation cannot choose that product and security boundary for maintainers.

options.title: Require staged core design
options.body: Split the work into reviewable owner-sponsored PRs for config/schema, state migration, protocol, runtime dispatch, and proof before merging any core behavior.

options.title: Accept exceptional broad PR
options.body: Maintainers explicitly own the large-PR, upgrade, security-boundary, and proof risk after conflicts and exact-head proof are resolved.

options.title: Close or defer
options.body: Decline this as core architecture for now and harvest narrower plugin/API gaps or docs as separate future work.

recommendation.title: Require staged core design
recommendation.body: Split the work into reviewable owner-sponsored PRs for config/schema, state migration, protocol, runtime dispatch, and proof before merging any core behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: martingarramon is the latest explicit human reviewer to carry forward partial LGTM on the continuation shape while blocking on head cleanliness.
